processing: Heated to stop oxidation, then rolled and dried, as with other green teas; individual estates differ and some use orthodox methods.
harvest_season: Java's tropical highland gardens are not tied to a single famous spring picking the way Chinese and Japanese gardens are, and no particular season is documented as the prized one.
appearance_dry: Dark, twisted green leaf, varying a lot by estate.
appearance_wet: Green leaf of medium size, varying by estate.
taste_profile: Varies by estate; generally described as fresh and light, with delicate herbal notes and a subtle astringency.

brewing.notes: A general green-tea starting point, brewed Western-style. Taste after two minutes and adjust for the estate.

vintage_note: There is no vintage culture around this tea. It is sold by estate and grade rather than by year, and as with any green tea, freshness is what counts, so look for a recent packing date.
description:
Java green tea means green tea grown on the Indonesian island of Java, mostly in the western highlands. It is a place name rather than one defined style, which is the first thing to know before buying.

Indonesia is mainly a black tea country, and green tea is the smaller side of it. West Java produces about two-thirds of the national tea crop, so much of the green tea comes from there too.

The cups vary. Java green is generally described as fresh and light with herbal notes, and West Java's Chakra Dewata estate has reportedly moved past greens once thought too smoky. Brew in cooler water first, since the style of the estate decides what you will get.

Buy by estate name and ask for a packing date.
history:
Tea in Indonesia is mainly a black tea story, and green tea is a minor part of Java's output, put at 10 to 15% by one tea merchant's account. Tea came to the island under Dutch colonial rule, and production later shifted towards domestic drinking.

Indonesian tea output has fallen from about 165 thousand tonnes in 2002 to about 125 thousand in 2022, and some Java estates have since invested in improving their greens.
